title: Isomorphisms descend along etale surjections
statement:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
let $u:U\to X$ be a surjective etale morphism of
separated finite-type
$k$-schemes, and let $\varphi:M\to N$ be a morphism of bounded
constructible complexes on $X$. If $Lu^*\varphi$ is an isomorphism,
then $\varphi$ is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Work at the finite coefficient $A=A_{E,n}$ fixed by the purity conventions. First regard $u:U\to X$ as a covering of $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$. Clause (1) of [det-pe-morphisms-etale-comparison] makes $u$ weakly etale. It is flat and locally of finite presentation by [def-weil-etale-morphism], so [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open] makes its underlying map open. For every affine open $V\subset X$, choose affine opens $W\subset u^{-1}(V)$ covering $u^{-1}(V)$. The open subsets $u(W)$ cover $V$ by surjectivity. The affine scheme $V$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], so finitely many of these images cover $V$. This is exactly the finite-affine-refinement covering condition in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Thus the singleton $\{u\}$ is a pro-etale cover. Empty $V$ uses the empty finite refinement.

source.place: proetale.tex Tags 0989 (proetale-definition-fpqc-covering) and 098B (proetale-lemma-etale-proetale); more-morphisms.tex Tag 094X (more-morphisms-lemma-when-weakly-etale); morphisms.tex Tag 01UA (morphisms-lemma-fppf-open); algebra.tex Tag 00E8 (algebra-lemma-quasi-compact)

proof.text: The site identification and constant-ring identification in [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] identify $U_{\mathrm{proet}}$ with $X_{\mathrm{proet}}/U$ and $A_U$ with $A_X|_U$. Under these identifications the inverse image along $u$ is sectionwise restriction, as follows directly from [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. For $W\to U$ in $U_{\mathrm{proet}}$, $W$ is also a weakly etale $X$-scheme. In the category $\mathcal I_W$ defining the inverse-image presheaf, the pair $(W,\gamma)$, where $\gamma:W\to U\times_XW$ is the graph of $W\to U$, is initial: the unique arrow to $(V,\phi:W\to U\times_XV)$ is $\operatorname{pr}_V\phi:W\to V$. Hence the opposite-indexed colimit is $F(W)$. These identifications commute with restrictions and sheaf morphisms; the resulting presheaf is already the restriction sheaf of [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. For the coefficient ring they fix each constant section, so they give precisely the canonical localized constant-ring identification, and the induced module pullback is $F|_U$ with its restricted action. This restriction is exact by [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact].

source.place: sites-modules.tex Tag 04IX (sites-modules-definition-localize-ringed-site), Tags 03DI (sites-modules-lemma-extension-by-zero) and 03DJ (sites-modules-lemma-extension-by-zero-exact); sites.tex Tag 06UM (sites-section-pullback); proetale.tex Tag 09A5 (proetale-section-morphism). The graph calculation explicitly identifies the scheme inverse image with localization restriction

proof.text: By the finite-level definition [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], $Lu^*$ is computed by applying this exact module inverse image termwise to any representative complex. The natural cohomology comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] therefore gives $\mathcal H^r(Lu^*K)\cong(\mathcal H^rK)|_U$ for every integer $r$. This holds for derived morphisms as well: the comparison is natural on complex maps, and its naturality equation remains true after inverting quasi-isomorphisms and composing the resulting roofs. For $K=M,N$ it identifies $\mathcal H^r(Lu^*\varphi)$ with the restriction of $h_r=\mathcal H^r(\varphi)$. The hypothesis on $Lu^*\varphi$ implies that every $h_r|_U$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: homology.tex Tag 010N (homology-lemma-exact-functor); derived.tex Tag 015F (derived-lemma-right-derived-exact-functor). Naturality on roofs is written out

proof.text: Fix $r$ and a test object $T\to X$ of the pro-etale site. The site base-change axiom in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] makes $T\times_XU\to T$ a cover. This object and its double overlap both map to $U$, so step 3 makes $h_r$ bijective on their sections. If two source sections on $T$ have the same image, their restrictions to $T\times_XU$ agree, hence they agree by the separatedness part of the sheaf equalizer axiom in that definition. Given a target section on $T$, invert $h_r$ on $T\times_XU$; the two restrictions of the inverse section to the double overlap agree because their images agree and $h_r$ there is injective. The sheaf axiom glues this section uniquely to $T$, and its image is the original section by separatedness. Thus $(h_r)_T$ is bijective for every $T$. Its inverse is additive, $A_X(T)$-linear and compatible with restrictions, since each of these equations follows after applying the injective map $(h_r)_T$. Consequently $h_r$ is an isomorphism of module sheaves. This also covers $X=\emptyset$: the empty covering forces a module sheaf on the empty object to have just its zero section.

source.place: sites.tex Tags 00VH (sites-definition-site), 00VM (sites-definition-sheaf-sets), 00VR (sites-definition-sheaf); proetale.tex Tag 098C (proetale-lemma-proetale) for cover base change. The local inverse and its overlap equation are explicit

proof.text: All the cohomology maps $\mathcal H^r(\varphi)$ are now isomorphisms. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology] to the abelian category of $A_X$-module sheaves on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$. It follows that $\varphi$ is invertible in the ambient derived category. The bounded constructible category is full, so this inverse is also an inverse in the category of the statement. This proves the required implication without any extra Tor-amplitude or etale-origin hypothesis.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-Codex-Q33-c6f9a7524 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: PASS for Q33/lem-pur-etale-iso-descent. The statement is unchanged and matches both blueprint snapshots exactly. Coefficients are A=A_{E,n} on X_proet (scope from def-pur-conventions), D^b_c is the full subcategory from def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility, and Lu^* is the finite-level pullback from def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom. The stmt_deps changes are justified: smooth morphisms are dropped, and separated comes from def-weil-proper-morphism. The delivery has no new nodes, proof_deps equals the union of the step uses, and the graph is acyclic. Step 1: étale implies weakly étale (det-pe (1), Stacks 094X(4)) and the map is open (UniversallyOpen.of_flat, 01UA); with quasi-compactness of V this is exactly the condition in Stacks 0989 (proetale.tex:2126). Step 2: I checked that the graph pair (W,γ) is initial in I_W, because pr_U∘φ is the structure map, so the colimit is F(W). Inverse image is therefore restriction, and that restriction is exact by lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact. Step 3: termwise representability is stated in the pullback definition, and homologyFunctorIso gives the natural comparison. Step 4 is an elementary sheaf-axiom gluing argument, complete and covering X=∅. Step 5: DerivedCategory.isIso_iff (HomologySequence.lean:88) plus fullness of D^b_c. The proof departs from the blueprint's geometric-stalk argument, and the departure is justified: lem-cbc-proetale-stalk-conservative (4) shows stalk non-conservativity, and its cover-locality clause (1) is a generalization only in the different Λ_{T,Proet} category, so it is not cited and same_as stays []. I accept the three declared tool uses: det-pe-morphisms-etale-comparison, lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization and lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact. No SGA source is cited.
